administration.teksAlignmentVintage: Pre-2019 Grade 8 Social Studies TEKS. Nine SE codes used on the 2018 and 2019 forms are no longer listed in TEA's current assessed curriculum (8.4(E), 8.6(D), 8.11(C), 8.12(D), 8.19(D), 8.19(E), 8.20(C), 8.26(C), 8.27(D)), and at least one surviving code (8.4(C)) covers different content today. TEA's label is recorded verbatim in teksAsPublished; see labelNote on affected items.

items.labelNote: TEA labelled this item 8.4(C) in 2018. The current assessed curriculum defines 8.4(C) as 'explain the issues surrounding important events of the American Revolution, including declaring independence; fighting the battles of Lexington and Concord, Saratoga, and Yorktown; enduring the winter at Valley Forge; and signing the Treaty of Paris of 1783', which does not cover the Articles of Confederation. This item's content maps to today's 8.15(B) 'summarize the strengths and weaknesses of the Articles of Confederation'. That remapping is OUR READING, not a TEA statement, and must be confirmed by a reviewer before the item is used against a current standard.

stimulus.title: Articles of Confederation
stimulus.text:
• Did not grant a federal power to tax or regulate commerce
• Did not establish a common currency
• Did not establish an executive or judicial branch

items.stem: What does this list suggest about the drafters of the Articles of Confederation?

options.text: They did not want a judicial system based upon that of Great Britain.
They feared that a strong central government would abuse its power.
They were uncertain that democracy would continue to be the best type of government.
They did not think that state governments could provide for the general welfare.

items.labelNote: 8.20(C) is not in TEA's current assessed curriculum, which lists only 8.20(A) and 8.20(B). This item's content (the Boston Tea Party as protest against taxation) sits under today's 8.20(B) 'analyze reasons for and the impact of selected examples of civil disobedience in U.S. history such as the Boston Tea Party'. That remapping is OUR READING, not a TEA statement.

stimulus.text: A number of brave & resolute men, determined to do all in their power to save their country from the ruin which their enemies had plotted, in less than four hours, emptied every chest of tea on board the three ships commanded by the captains Hall, Bruce, and Coffin, amounting to 342 chests, into the sea!! without the least damage done to the ships or any other property. The matters and owners are well pleas’d that their ships are thus clear’d; and the people are almost universally congratulating each other on this happy event.

items.stem: The actions described in this excerpt were carried out in order to —

protest a ban on selling beverages in the colonies
